📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 players progress through the plot and explore beyond the sunny shores of Key Lento, bunny boiler Mandy has been left behind.

It’s all about Delights’ resident goth girl Vicki now!

The character plays a bit-part during Chapter 2, and she’s swiftly become a fave among PS5 players for her husky voice and no-nonsense attitude.

Writing on X, one fan put it simply: “Oh yeah we on Vicki now, I don’t even know who Mandy is!”.

Some have even taken to social media stalking the dancer on Snapmatic:.

Simping aside, Vicki may actually sound familiar because her voice actor is Taryn Manning, who had a pretty major role as Tiffany ‘Pennsatucky’ Doggett in Orange Is the New Black.

The 48-year-old actress has also starred in a variety of other highlights like Sons of Anarchy, and has even had parts in movies like Hustle & Flow and the 8-Mile.

There are a lot of characters to keep track of in GTA 6, but Vicki is definitely one that stuck with me, largely because she’s pivotal to one of my favourite missions in the game.

(I won’t spoil that here, but if you’re grinning you’ll probably know which one I’m referring to.).

I’m not going to get into the Vicki vs Mandy debate, but I’m sure social media will have its final say eventually.

#74664. Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games.
  • Industry observers note that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95.
  • Microsoft, all the while, were taking notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.

Industry observers note that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95. At E3 later that May, Microsoft demonstrated the Strategic Commander for the first time with SimCity 3000, while promoting its potential for other such games as Diablo II, Warcraft III, and Baldur's Gate II. This was all taking place during the so-called 'Golden Age of Real-Time Strategy Games,' which spanned roughly from the mid-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was when the RTS genre was at the peak of its mainstream popularity, and we fans were devoted to mastering its intricacies in any way we could to have a competitive edge.

Microsoft, all the while, were taking notes. "The team conceived the Strategic Commander in the late 1990s," Carl Ledbetter - then Industrial Design Manager for Microsoft's PC Hardware Group, now Head of Design for Xbox Devices - recalls to me. "As RTS games grew in popularity, we saw an interesting opportunity to design a newly introduced physical interface around a new interaction model. The idea was for it to be used left-handed in concert with right-hand PC desktop mouse control. We wanted to enable players to perform faster with more fluidity, comfort, optimised control placement for multiple hand sizes, simplicity of set-up, and ease of programming.".

Sources indicate that for Ledbetter and co. to realise this ambition, the Strategic Commander was designed as a unique combination of mouse, joystick, and gamepad. To manage the increasing complexities of the RTS games of the day, it came equipped with six programmable buttons, three shift buttons, and a three-position profile switch. Back then, these atypical features provided an unprecedented 72 possible key combinations across various configurations, all at the tip of our stubby little fingers. Better yet, it allowed us to toggle between three pre-configured profiles at a time, so that we could switch up our configurations on the fly depending on which stage of an RTS match we were in.

On release, contemporary reviewers acknowledged its originality, with critics like ActiveWin's Julien Jay describing it as "probably the most innovative (with the GameVoice) and revolutionary" peripheral designed specifically for strategy players. Others, like Neoseeker's Arnel Lim, suggested that it might’ve gone overboard with its customisation options, saying "you won't use anywhere close to all of them," in reference to the controller's programmable key combinations. Either way, the Strategic Commander failed to supplant conventional peripherals in the hands of most RTS players, and it was discontinued in 2003. As was the rest of the original SideWinder line, owing to declining sales and the industry-wide shift toward standard M+K setups for all PC games and genres.

However, unlike so many of its Microsoft-made siblings, this was not the end for the Strategic Commander. Niche as it was, it went on to enjoy a surprisingly long post-shelf life, one that was stretched out by a dedicated cult following - and that continues to this day. But why? Why, after all these years, is this forgotten peripheral from a discontinued line maintaining such a enthusiastic fanbase, years after the industry around it had written it off as a failure?

According to recent reports, the answer lies in software and OS compatibility, as much as the hardware's own appeal. Andreas Weis was the developer of one of the first unofficial patches for the Strategic Commander, allowing players to keep on using it even after the original software stopped being compatible with newer versions the Windows. By that point, the device was a decade old, and well into 'official' obsolescence, yet Weis still answered the call of the Strategic Commander's righteously frustrated - if numerically few - fans. "There was a lot of interest back in the early 2010s in software patches to keep the Strategic Commander functional when the original software for the Strategic Commander stopped working," he explains. "Consumers were asking around on internet forums about how to get it to work on Windows 7 and Vista machines. Since I was studying computer science at the time, I was quite interested in reverse-engineering, and I hacked together a simple tool that would cover my use cases for the device.".

In a recent development, in the years that followed, other patches were released to keep the Strategic Commander operational, the most notable of which was Philip Merwarth’s Strategic Engine software in 2013. Unfortunately, they weren’t open-source. Worse was that the protocol for programming the Strategic Commander wasn’t documented anywhere online in a way that was accessible for people. This is why Weis realized that he could make a unique contribution.

It has been revealed that "I polished my old prototype code for the Strategic Commander software patch and released it as a library, so that other people could use it to write their own applications for programming the tool," he notes. "As for me, I released one application that made use of the library publicly, the vJoy feeder application, which allows the device to be used with games that support joystick inputs." Curiously, Weis, by this time and like many others, had found other applications for a device with such a specific selling point, and even continues to use the Strategic Commander sparingly in 2026.

Sources indicate that "The production quality of Microsoft hardware at the time was just top-notch, and I love the design of the old SideWinder devices, which is why I did not just throw the thing out when the software stopped working," he tells me. "It was worth keeping around to find new uses for it over the years, and I eventually realized that it makes quite a nice addition to a HOTAS (Hands-On Throttle And Stick) setup, where I could put actions that aren’t time-critical and don't fit well on the throttle on the Strategic Commander instead. For example, when I’m playing Elite Dangerous in VR, I’d put actions like deploying the landing gear on the Strategic Commander to free up buttons on the throttle for actions that were more relevant for combat.".

When looking back at the history of Microsoft’s SideWinder line, it’s easy to call the Strategic Commander a failed experiment, given the fact that most of us are still using the same standard mouse-and-keyboard setup to play RTS games. However, the central premise behind its design philosophy was that the interface between a player and a game could be redesigned to cater to specific genre quirks, and decades following its release, it’s still maintained a coalition of loyal users: some RTS players who believed the Strategic Commander really pulled it off, and those found other uses for the device in other flavours of PC game. And with the issue of modern compatibility, a roadblock for so much retro hardware, bypassed by homemade patches, both camps can continue twisting and clicking their Strategic Commanders unimpeded.

All the same, I wonder if it might have basked in more conventional success, had Microsoft made more forward-thinking decisions. The Strategic Commander has proven over the years that its unprecedented customisation had applications far beyond what Ledbetter’s team had envisioned, and once the popularity of RTS games settled down, other, similar click-heavy subgenres like MOBAs and Real-Time Tactics got significant as well. Would a more officially maintained, potentially refined Strategic Commander model have served those crowds? I think it might. The narrow focus on RTS games may have also hurt the device's since-demonstrated broader appeal; if Microsoft had fully capitalised on this customisation selling point by communicating its benefits to everyone, not just those playing the single most popular PC genre at the time, it could have provided the blueprint for a proper, long-lived alternative to controllers, mice, and keyboards.

Alas, gaming history is littered with revolutionary peripherals that failed to actually revolutionise the industry surrounding them. The Strategic Commander is no different, but for the fact that it’s had this surprisingly long post-shelf life - and, as a result, the opportunity for insight into what could have been done to salvage the its failures. Still, that unexpected longevity can provide come comfort to the Strategic Commander's creators, as well as its lingering people.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the design made sense for its time, especially with the rising popularity of RTS games," Ledbetter reflects. "Looking back, I would have liked more time to test and refine the Strategic Commander. I’m proud of what we brought to market, and I’m glad to know that it remains beloved by many players to this day.".

World of Warcraft: Forever completionists push back as Blizzard gives them a powerful toy and then prepares to take it away

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole newly introduced world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect.
  • That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game.
  • In a recent development, on occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole newly introduced world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

In a recent development, on occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

Sources indicate that this is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators remarked in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

They aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

"Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

The battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both crucial to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later update for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of new quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked.
  • It has been revealed that the Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub.
  • The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look.

It has been revealed that the Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio, which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name.

The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.

Look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.

You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.

The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

In a recent development, head upstairs to the second floor and enter the Jack of Hearts recording studio. Pass through the lobby and into the control room, then you'll see the Sniper of Perle poster lying on the table beside a fan.

Once you arrive at the nightclub, head through the entrance corridor and look at the back wall. The poster is right there, and one quick scan is all it takes to unlock The Vault's playlist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Every new Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

It has been revealed that "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

Recent findings suggest that while Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

It has been revealed that "I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

Industry observers note that GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

If you'd like to reminisce a bit before the long-awaited game finally hits, you can check out our favourite Grand Theft Auto pieces Eurogamer's published over the years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

It has been revealed that the class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

The trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a fresh motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

"But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

In a recent development, you know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which currently looks likely to last until at least 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is almost over. Years after Robert Downey Jr.'s return as Doctor Doom was announced on stage at San Diego Comic-Con, we're on the precipice of Doom's MCU debut, and to celebrate, we're taking a Stark Tech time machine back to 2018, when Total Film reported from the set of Avengers: Infinity War.

Pulled from the May 2018 glitch of Total Film magazine, this time capsule feature is a fascinating snapshot of the MCU ahead of its biggest (and arguably best) movie, with candid insight from Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chadwick Boseman, Tom Holland, Elizabeth Olsen, the Russo brothers and many, many more.

Avengers: Doomsday is one of this year's (and any year's) most exciting upcoming movies, and there's no better time to revisit a crucial chapter on the road to Doomsday. When you're done reading this time capsule set report, be sure to check out our own experience revisiting the movie, as we consider why Avengers: Infinity War is "essential viewing" ahead of Avengers: Doomsday. But for now, let's take a trip to the set of Avengers: Infinity War….

Recent findings suggest that pinewood Atlanta Studios, 2017. Total Film is on the top-secret set of Avengers: Infinity War, one of the few remaining instalments in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Phase Three, and the culmination of the 18 previous MCU movies to date. It's the most ambitious team-up yet for a studio that pioneered the concept of assembling disparate heroes onscreen in an 'expanded universe'.

At Chris 'Star-Lord' Pratt's estimate, there are 22 superheroes uniting to face down the ultimate major bad. What TF witnesses on Stage 9 is just a hint of the carnage that intergalactic villain Thanos (played by Josh Brolin, via motion-capture) will wreak when he comes to Earth to enact his grand plan. Fire. Twisted metal. Fallen trees. Soil and gravel everywhere.

Crew members ensure that the fires are burning just where they need to be, as dozens of cast and stunt performers prepare to run purposefully out of a trench for a slow-motion shot. Details are scarce as to what's actually going on, but it's fair to assume something massive has occurred. Avengers rub shoulders with Guardians, as Wakandan warriors take up arms alongside characters who look like they've stepped through a portal from another realm entirely.

In a recent development, mark Ruffalo – in strategically spotted skin-tight pyjamas – has a mast attached to his head to indicate the Hulk's eyeline and the scale of his CGI avatar. By any measure – creative, logistical, and presumably budgetary – this is the biggest Marvel movie yet. Hydraulic canisters hiss, and bangs break out when action's called and the cameras roll.

In a recent development, when we later catch up with the cast, snatching chats with handfuls of Avengers at a time, their bloodied and bruised faces attest to the trouble the superteam has found themselves in. But for now, the sheer scale of this diorama of destruction is jaw-dropping. "It's truly like herding cats," Captain America actor Chris Evans jokes to TF of the enormo-cast. "I look at the first AD, this poor guy. It's just hard to get everybody focused.".

During a break in filming, writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely (of all three Captain America movies) explain how they solved the challenge of incorporating so many heroes into one film: making genocidal Titan warlord Thanos the main character. Having been teased since the mid-credits sting of 2012's The Avengers, Thanos is finally taking his place in the sun.

In a recent development, "The thing that separates it from other Avengers movies for me is that the antagonist is the main character," notes McFeely. "So in many ways, this is Thanos's movie. It was the smartest way for us to accommodate all the characters and honour this [villain] that Marvel's been teasing for so long.".

When asked how high the stakes are, McFeely offers, "Is the universe high enough for you?" The Mad Titan has some high-minded ideals about how the universe should be, and his proposal involves wiping out about half of its inhabitants. In order to set his plan in motion, he needs six MacGuffins that have been seeded throughout the series so far: the Infinity Stones, which will slot into his golden gauntlet and give him godlike powers.

It has been revealed that "He wants six Infinity Stones," explains Markus. "And once you get them, you can do whatever you want." It goes some way towards explaining why quite such an exhaustive roster of heroes is required to even begin to fight off such an omnipotent foe and his "elite squad," the Black Order. But, following the events of Civil War, the divided superteam are at a low ebb.

"I mean, the whole point of doing Civil War was that they enter this movie fractured and separated, and that will play a very integral part of the film," explains Joe Russo, one half of the director duo, the Russo brothers. In Infinity War, the core Avengers – Iron Man, Cap, Thor, Black Widow, Hulk, et al. – will be joined by Black Panther, Spider-Man, Doctor Strange, the Guardians Of The frickin' Galaxy, and more.

So, after the head-to-head in Civil War, has the relationship between Iron Man and Cap improved at all? "I don't know that it could have gotten any worse," considers Evans when we catch him between takes, clad in his Cap suit, sans helmet and chest-piece, his face dirtied from the day's action. Robert Downey Jr. – the Iron Man star who was integral to kicking off the entire MCU – concurs.

According to recent reports, "I wouldn't say he does [get on with Cap]," Downey Jr. explains, holding court with the laid-back confidence of a talk show host. "I'm saying that because Thanos is the threat. I don't think it can be underestimated. It's not just what Josh Brolin is bringing to his portrayal of it, but there's something about it where we've all agreed that this is the sum of all of our fears. It's like Gestalt therapy at this point.".

At the moment dressed in a camo T-shirt and hoodie, the (fake) blood above RDJ's eyebrow attests to a pretty physical form of therapy. "I think because the threat has risen to a new level – which is really saying something – that whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do," he continues. "So I think that's a bit of a new thing. So it's like, 'Can these disparate heroes get along after all?'".

Chris Hemsworth – out of his Thor costume and wearing a dressing gown over a black T-shirt and jogging bottoms – attests to the scale of the threat. "I think that [Thanos is] the strongest thing we've ever faced, his force," he states in his Aussie baritone. "And it brings out a whole other level of us, I think, and another stage or journey we need to embark on.".

According to recent reports, tom Holland strolls over to join Downey Jr. and Hemsworth. Munching on a banana to keep up his calorie intake, he's clad in black mo-cap pyjamas (a requirement of his upgraded Spider-Man suit), with a puffer jacket to keep him warm in the empty neighbouring soundstage we're now occupying, and he's sporting a bloodied nose.

Sources indicate that keen to avoid dropping spoilers (as he's been known to do on social media), Holland's staying tight-lipped about Peter Parker's journey, although he does tease that "he matures a lot", before Downey Jr. adds with a sly grin: "Things you wouldn't expect are endured.".

Dishing out the cuts and bruises is Thanos, who'll draw all the other characters into his orbit. Having a bad guy at the forefront will mark a real change of pace for the typically hero-heavy MCU, and means that Thanos needs the requisite depth to carry the film.

In a recent development, "We were considering showing his backstory," claims Anthony Russo, "but ultimately felt it wasn't necessary for the movie. However, the movie is told from his point of view. I think it's a very interesting space for an audience to be in, because every villain thinks they're the hero of their own story. We thought it'd become compelling to track a villain's point of view through a movie.".

Anthony Russo goes on to call Brolin's performance "stunning", explaining that he brings "an intensity and a violence, but also at the same time, a charm and a sensitivity. It's a very complicated character. He's at times despicable and horrifying, and at other times oddly empathetic.".

Because the threat has risen to a new level, whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do.

Recent findings suggest that having Brolin on set (albeit in those unavoidable mo-cap pyjamas) gives the digital character added heft, as well as providing the actors with something to work against. "It really is mind-blowing how sensitive a performance we can translate into a CG character now, and how much of Josh's performance is in that character," adds Joe Russo.

Sources indicate that "He brings some humanity to something that could just be a one-dimensional villain," states Karen Gillan, her friendly Scottish accent bizarrely contrasting with the menacing blue makeup she's covered in to play Gamora. "I can't look him in the eye, but I hear his voice," says Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman of working opposite Brolin when he's mo-capping an eight-foot-tall character. "He's right there.".

Yes, Black Panther and his Wakandan allies will play a crucial part in Infinity War, with the third-act battle set to go down on his home turf. Given the astonishing success of T'Challa's recent solo movie, his presence will only heighten the anticipation for Infinity War. "Being able to bring that energy into Infinity War, and that dimensionality and those themes into our movie, it's a gift for us," beams Joe Russo.

When we speak to Boseman on set, he looks like one cool cat in his full Panther get-up (minus the mask), even with a long coat draped over his shoulders.

In a recent development, "How does he fit in as an Avenger?" Boseman considers. "I don't know if it's a situation where it's like a club that you join. I think the fact that Wakanda, to a certain degree, opens up a newly introduced place for the Avengers to fit. As opposed to him fitting into the Avengers, he opens up a new space. And that's pretty much all I can say." That charismatic chuckle booms. "That's all I can say!".

"It's like Voltron, you know what I mean?" quips Evans of the characters uniting. "This other franchise starts doing well, and they start forming one giant thing. It's really exciting.".

Sources indicate that benedict Cumberbatch's Doctor Strange will also play a key role, being brought into the fold with Wong (Benedict Wong) via Tony Stark and Bruce Banner/Hulk (Ruffalo). Holland's Spidey also returns after high-school spin Homecoming. Hot on the heels of Thor: Ragnarok, the gut-bustingly funny threequel that saw Thor and Hulk flexing their comedic muscles, that duo will find themselves in a slightly more serious predicament this time out.

In a recent development, "God knows I tried [to be funny]," laughs Ruffalo, his face still dotted with mo-cap markers. "It's the Russo brothers, so it's not quite as comedic. Although the fact that Vision's forehead bears one of the Infinity Stones that Thanos wants might impact their courtship. "That's one of the fun things that's going to happen in these two movies, those introductions of those characters to each other," says Don 'War Machine' Cheadle, sporting the unofficial uniform of, yep, mo-cap PJs. It has been revealed that of course, franchise stalwart Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) returns, as does former Winter Soldier Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Falcon (Anthony Mackie) and Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), who has been seen sporting a new mohawk but has been absent from all trailers so far. Although the one group of characters who could really shake things up are the Guardians Of The Galaxy, the ragtag team of spacefarers who have little regard for traditional heroics, and strut to their own mixtape beat. From the first trailer, when Thor spies the bunch of a-holes and asks, "Who the hell are you guys?", the chemistry seemed inevitable.

When we talk to Star-Lord himself, Chris Pratt, he's wearing his signature red leather jacket and also has a dirtied, bloody face.

"The stakes have never been higher," he says between forkfuls of lunch from a Tupperware pot (the cast and crew are working 'French hours' and eating on the fly). "All the movies have led towards this. You couldn't just have any old standard villain. You have to have the one villain who touched every one of those characters' storylines.".

"Well, I sensed glory, but I will tell you this: I just have such pride. Really, honestly, the main thing is, I think we really have become this oddball family that genuinely looks after and cares for each other, and supports each other. So that's a first for me. The other thing is, none of us would be here at this stage without Joss [Whedon]. Because he did a proof-of-concept execution that was monumental. But then there's been a quantum – literally – shift in the way that things are going now, where all these different franchises are on the horizon, and they're bringing upcoming energy, and some of us are maybe tapping out or going away. Who knows what the future is? But the task is yet to be completed. I don't think I've been hoisted up in a chair and marched around yet like I deserve, but we'll see.".

According to recent reports, what could make Infinity War (and Avengers: Endgame ) so monumental is that it arrives at the time when the MCU is welcoming a lot of fresh blood, while older contracts might be coming to an end. This could be a time of metamorphosis and reinvigoration. Naturally, cast and crew avoid spoilers, but they do promise that the roster is in for a shake-up, and we could see some permanent exits.

For all the talk of death, the atmosphere on set isn't morose, and the camaraderie of the cast is evident. After all, they've had enough films to forge a bond on, and they're clearly enjoying being part of such an expansive repertory.

"Like meeting [the Guardians] as Thor, but also as Chris, was equally as exciting and latest, and it brought in a whole different energy. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.
  • Sources indicate that the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

Sources indicate that the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

Sources indicate that at the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

As the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Recent findings suggest that those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

In a recent development, "We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar noted at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way.".

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

It has been revealed that split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

Recent findings suggest that this new mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

Recent findings suggest that as for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an concern for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming update, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history". But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "indicates a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off.".

In a recent development, it might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

In a recent development, it's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This glitch was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July, claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 introduces.

"99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team.".

Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction.".

Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.

"I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Naughty Dog’s Michael Barclay – whose credits include Uncharted: The Lost Legacy and The Last of Us 2 – says he’s “made video games for 19 years and GTA 6 appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child”.

Rockstar’s latest open world release is by far the best-looking game ever made, even if it is locked to 30fps on PS5 hardware.

And it’s being treated like witchcraft by devs, who naturally have a greater appreciation for the feats on display.

Barclay, who’s currently working on next year’s Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, continued:.

“I'm always astonished that [Rockstar’s] environmental lighting is mostly dynamic and looks as good if not better than most baked lighting.”.

In really, really simple terms, baked lighting is a game development technique used to save computational cost by calculating light and shadow data in advance.

The downside to this is that it’s fixed, but obviously given the ever-changing nature of GTA 6’s sandbox, it needs to have a dynamic solution.

Barclay is saying that GTA 6’s dynamic lighting matches and even surpasses those pre-determined solutions in many scenarios, making it a real accomplishment.

These comments triggered discussion from various other industry professionals, including Tim Soret from Odd Tales, the makers of The Last Night, who outlined some of his thoughts on the title:.

GTA 6 sets a standard so unfathomably high I do wonder at what point it’ll ever be topped.

I suppose raising the bar like this will motivate the many other talented devs around the world, but not every studio will have access to the time and the estimated $1 billion budget that allowed Rockstar to deliver this.

Either way, it’s clear industry professionals are utterly blown away by what the studio has delivered here.

Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • Sources indicate that the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

Sources indicate that the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

It makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

Thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

Sources indicate that it's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

In terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock latest rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make new, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight years on since the launch of its first chapter, Deltarune seems to be rapidly approaching completion. With five chapters already released for Toby Fox's sequel to the beloved RPG Undertale, two more are expected before the game is complete. And according to Deltarune creator Toby Box, not only is chapter 6 close to being finished, but work has also already begun on chapter 7.

Fox provided the status update in his most recent newsletter. Kicking off with a general note that chapter 6 is "progressing well", Fox explains that "the game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. He further elaborates that "all the maps, events and battles exist", with the exception of one optional event that's still being worked on.

As a result, the Deltarune team is now at the point where they feel comfortable commencing localisation and preliminary testing. Fox clarifies, however, that full testing won't begin just yet, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation". Indeed, while chapter 6 is progressing rapidly, players shouldn't expect an imminent release. "Even though chapter 6 is a rather short chapter, I would like it to be as good as possible. I won't be able to rush this," Fox points out.

Sources indicate that as for Chapter 7, Fox says that development has "only just started". Designers who have finished their Chapter 6 work have moved on to work on the latest chapter, while Fox has shared some of the dialogue and events with the Deltarune team. "Just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading. I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens," he explained, adding that "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.".

It's impressive progress, considering that chapter 5 released in June. Then again, development of Deltarune has accelerated rapidly since 2025, when Fox released chapters 3 and 4 of the game in the same year. The launch of chapter 5 also demonstrated just how much fans want to see the story through, as 300,000 concurrent players flocked to Steam to check out the latest chunk of the game.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

The revision in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

As part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. It has been revealed that unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that strategy release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the manufacturer has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental issues.

It has been revealed that unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

Sources indicate that the grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

  • As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

Recent findings suggest that the manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

The effects of the technology on gamemakers, such as "directly and indirectly replacing workers", "worker fatigue, cognitive decline and burnout", and "a marked decline in junior positions in the industry" are listed as core harms to be avoided and fought against, with the manifesto also noting that it also "removes a sense of ownership from workers [...] the things they produce no longer feel like they have the workers' stamp on them, and therefore they can no longer take pride in them." As it states, "games are best made by people.".

In a recent development, the manifesto goes on to explains the unions' stance that genAI is "sold to employers as an alternative to workers", and its "predisposition towards sycophancy and lack of real world context can lead to an increase in unreasonable, damaging requests when used by employers to set policy, timescales, workloads, etc., as well as to task expansion and a general degradation of conditions." In addition, its nature as a tool built on the theft of stolen third-party data is highlighted as an inherent danger, and the so-called loophole in only training models on internal data is equally highlighted as resulting in employees and creators rarely being credited or compensated for their work that is fed into the machine. This glitch also ties into the inherent implicit and explicit discrimination that exists in genAI content due to datasets' "intrinsic and exclusionary Western bias that limits diversity and marginalises non-dominant languages, cultures, and ethnicities", which leads to "a homogenisation of culture.".

As for action, the manifest recommends that workers should "avoid usage of genAI services whenever possible", "distance yourself from genAI usage", and "make it clear to your employer why you do not want to use genAI", as well as, of course, to "organise. Unionise. Do it now, not when it is too late and you are already under threat." Similarly, employers are recommended to "ensure that no worker is required to use genAI", and to "disallow the use of genAI in the firm code of conduct, even for early stages of development." Finally, for consumers, it simply advises to "support games made without genAI", and to "be vocal about disliking genAI in games.".

It's an incredibly clear and concise statement that calls to mind the statement made by a selection of IGF jurors on the state of genAI in the industry and their decision not to vote for any game that uses genAI in any capacity. As both of these statements are joined in saying, "we do not have to accept the use of genAI to make video games; it is not inevitable.".

World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.
  • It has been revealed that this exploit was swiftly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a currently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits.
  • According to recent reports, this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

It has been revealed that this exploit was swiftly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a currently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

According to recent reports, this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

Recent findings suggest that for an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Sources indicate that looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point.".

In a recent development, flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream says enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked.".

You may be wondering why this is such a massive deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

The counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

Sources indicate that as of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the big question.

GTA 6 is a cozy game

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that GTA 6 has dragged us out of our comfort zone here at PC Gamer, forcing us to play a game on a console.
  • This seems to be the consensus among my colleagues in crime, who I've gathered to share their favourite parts of GTA 6's early game—fishing, interior decorating and chilling with some problematic faves.
  • In a recent development, I've been playing GTA since the top-down days, but with every new incarnation of Rockstar's criminal caper I've been drifting away from the action and learning to appreciate life in the slow lane.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that GTA 6 has dragged us out of our comfort zone here at PC Gamer, forcing us to play a game on a console. A tragedy! But it's OK because GTA 6, as you may have heard, is rather good. And it's especially good when the shooting stops and you just get to hang out with your weird crime pals.

This seems to be the consensus among my colleagues in crime, who I've gathered to share their favourite parts of GTA 6's early game—fishing, interior decorating and chilling with some problematic faves.

In a recent development, I've been playing GTA since the top-down days, but with every new incarnation of Rockstar's criminal caper I've been drifting away from the action and learning to appreciate life in the slow lane. I have two wolves inside me, and in GTA 6, with its potent life sim DNA, the wolf who just wants to knock back beers with my virtual buddies is soundly beating the one who keeps screaming, "Do more crime!".

In a recent development, guys, GTA 6 is a cosy game. It's a restorative holiday. I wake up and meditate with my partner before she goes to work. I do a bit of lifting. Watch some TV. Then it's time for a drive. Maybe I'll buy a new shirt or get a tasteful and definitely not monstrously-huge slab of ink to honour my son at the grotty tattoo parlour. Then the ocean beckons me—it's fishing time! I take some snaps of my catch so I can brag about it to my best friend. Oh, Brian is calling? He wants me to do more crimes? Sorry, Bri! I'm going treasure hunting in my boat and sending my partner thirst traps.

Recent findings suggest that it's all just so pleasantly wholesome. Playing videogames with Cal, fixing up the house with Lucia, doing errands for my eccentric neighbour. Sure, that time I agreed to steal her best friend's mobility scooter definitely falls into the crime caper category, but only slightly. That's been my favourite chase so far—inching down the road while an old lady slowly jogs after me.

GTA's combat is serviceable and sometimes a whole lotta fun (I beat up some dudes with a basketball last night), and I've had a hoot getting stuck into Leonida's coke smuggling scene, but it feels like GTA's most impressive innovations are found in the quieter parts—the way it's constantly getting you to build relationships on your off hours, the wee nods to roleplaying, the believability and vibrancy of Leonida. This has been a crucial part of GTA since the San Andreas days, but in GTA 6 it feels like it's become the focus. I'm extremely happy about this.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has so many fun, small ways to make standing around and listening to dialogue more immersive that it almost makes the parts where you actually have to pick up a gun and shoot feel weirdly stagnant. I love the missions where you're just shooting the shit—building furniture, buying beers for a pal going through it, playing videogames. I love that I can do things like pour myself a coffee or light a cigarette while I'm having a conversation with another character. I love that I can construct a whole morning routine where I work out, go for a shower, and pick my outfit for the day.

In a recent development, the 'quieter' moments are where Leonida and its inhabitants really shine. I've lost track of how many times I've forgone a mission in favour of stopping to engage in all of the little random encounters—like a woman harassing a drive-thru worker for cheese, or a guy who is so lawsuit-brained that he ventures back into his burning vehicle for a bigger payday. Dilly-dallying has never felt so good.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's fishing is pretty much unchanged from Red Dead Redemption 2, but I'm already doing it a lot more here because of Jason and Cal's ongoing fishing rivalry. We're catching somewhat significant fish, sending pics, and talking trash about how the other guy will never find a bigger one.

It's wonderful and totally optional, which is indicative of how GTA 6 imbues many activities that would otherwise just 'be there' with social incentives. Every task, chore, or hobby involves talking to someone or sharing your day, and yes, it's pretty cosy. And if you're looking for a better fishing reel, check the sports shop near Jason's house.

I love when a game gives you a broad objective to just go earn money—also known as pulling a Baldur's Gate 2. It's a great excuse to diverge from the main path, to actually spend time getting to know a place without feeling pressured to progress the story in some meaningful way. In my last session, I spent most of my time exploring old shipwrecks for treasure—just me, my diving gear, some lost relics and the occasional shark.

It has been revealed that which, sure, it's an open world game with a lot of things to do on the side. This is not exactly a revelation. But, as always with Rockstar, the difference is in the production value and the attention to detail. The level of immersion is such that it doesn't feel like you're ticking off tasks on a checklist, because everything happens through the filter of Jason and Lucia's day-to-day. Every journey distracts you with surprising interactions and interesting things to check out. Every text message and social post builds the illusion of a place rich with life and detail. And so, yeah, when you finally decide to go do a main quest and the bullets start flying, it's almost disappointing to be back doing the things GTA has done for decades.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A new Fallout game is indeed on the way, but it's not what you're expecting. Bethesda's next post-apocalyptic project is in fact a cat-themed hidden object game.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this week, a listing from the Australian Classifications Board accidentally spilled information about a game called A Wasteland Full of Cats. The now-deleted description let slip that it's a hidden object game - think Where's Wally/Waldo - where you need to find cats in some of the series' underground Vaults and the dangerous radioactive lands outside.

"You play as one of the cats in the Vault. One day there is an accident in the Vault and all of the cats who live there escape out into the Wasteland. It is up to you with the help of some NPCs you meet along the way to find them and return them to the Vault," according to the listing.

"This game has 14 locations, 33 rooms + a vault of recognizable levels from the Fallout franchise with light puzzle mechanics that uncover some hidden levels that aren't required to finish the game. There is a final boss fight where the player has to shoot some Rad roaches in order to save the last remaining cats and humans. This game will be part of Devcats 'Full of Cats' series of cats and plays like the other games in the series. This game is in partnership with Bethesda and the Fallout franchise.".

According to recent reports, it didn't take long for series owner Bethesda to confirm the leak, either. "Cat's out of the bag," the studio writes on social media, explaining that it's partnered with non-profit animal charity Dallas Pets Alive and developer Devcat Games on the "Fallout-inspired adventure.".

There's no trailer or release date yet, but Bethesda says it'll "have more to share soon.".

If finding hard-to-spot felines sounds like your vibe, Devcat Games has a ton of other games in the Full of Cats series, whether you're into exploring castles or flats or outer space.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Industry observers note that A Wasteland Full of Cats might not be the Fallout game fans were expecting after the tech giant formally announced remasters for Fallout 3 and Fallout: Fresh Vegas, alongside a new game from Obsidian Entertainment, but it sounds like a cute stop over along the way. Fallout 5 is also in early pre-production.

Fallout 5 being set outside the US "could be amazing," former Bethesda lead says, even if Todd Howard has previously suggested it's not happening.
