📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It turns out Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, did successfully manage a payout from the producers of You Can See Everything, which has been crushing it on the 2026 movie schedule. However, the money isn’t going to him or Holmes. Instead, it’s going to charity. The details are still a little murky, but we do have more understanding of what went down after the scene in the movie where he brings it up and the card at the end that explains he changed his mind and wasn’t going to profit from the movie. Given how substantial a box office hit ($89 million and counting) the A24 release has been, it's probably a nice chunk of change. So what is going on? Here’s what we know.

One of the more controversial aspects of the production of You Can See Everything was Evans negotiating a payout with execs from A24 and the movie's co-directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The scene, which sees Evans asking for money after Holmes has left the room, has been a topic of conversation among fans of the film. Even lawyers have chimed in on how it could affect the judgment against Holmes, who owes somewhere north of $400 million in restitution after her conviction on fraud crimes.

In the scene, everyone agrees that Evans (and presumably Holmes) will be paid for their appearances. Then, at the end, a card appears informing the audience that Evans backed off this deal and wouldn’t be paid. Now, a new report in The Hollywood Reporter has clarified it. According to the article, Evans is earning money on the backend, but that money is reportedly going to a children’s charity. The article did not specify which charity.

Industry observers note that the outlet also confirmed with A24 that a deal had been struck, but neither the outlet’s sources nor A24 revealed how much the charity would be getting or what percentage of the backend was negotiated. The film is closing in on $100 million at the box office, and it's sure to earn more when it hits VOD sometime in the near future (the exact date is still not confirmed). That’s to say nothing about whatever money the film will earn when it moves to HBO Max, likely in early 2027.

Sources indicate that this is yet another saga in a movie that is full of intrigue both on-screen and off. It is also another wrinkle in trying to determine what is true and what is not. That question is at the core of the movie, and it seems even now, weeks after its release and years after Evans and Holmes were filmed before she reported to prison in 2023. That question is still lingering in every aspect. I’ve said before that this movie is like an onion, and this is one more layer getting peeled away, but it’s only offering up another layer that is just as fascinating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

Industry observers note that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely upcoming modes, the possibilities are vast.".

According to recent reports, the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

It has been revealed that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a massive visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Industry observers note that beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game debuts.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Latest York.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

Sources indicate that it's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Newly introduced Zealand trick for eager players to try.

The version 3.4 update for Zenless Zone Zero, dubbed “The Finality of the Day,” will launch on December 2, developer miHoYo confirmed.

Here is an overview of the enhancement, via miHoYo:.

The story of the Sky Island of Roscaelifer reaches its final climax, as Sunbringer, a new Void Hunter and the first Enchainer Agent, joins the fight. The new version also kicks off the Zenless Zone Zero × Honkai: Star Rail collaboration, introducing two crossover Agents, Robin and Kafka, along with themed events. It also brings new combat gameplay, updates to permanent game modes, and a variety of version rewards.

In a recent development, in Version 3.4, Roscaelifer’s main story is about to reach its climax. From the Bangboo corruption incident to High Ambitions Corp.’s invasion, the Proxies and their allies have weathered crisis after crisis together. Now, the enemy has stepped out of the shadows, and Roscaelifer faces a decisive battle for its very survival. For the first time, the three Sunbringers — Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda—will fight side-by-side, joining the Proxies to take on a formidable foe and defend Roscaelifer. New characters and menacing enemies are taking the stage, while the arrival of an unexpected character leaves even more mysteries hanging over this new chapter. How will this storm change the fate of the Celestial Nexus? What trials await the Proxies and their allies? All will be revealed in “The Finality of the Day.”.

Recent findings suggest that once this version update goes live, Sunbringer, leader of Roscaelifer, joins the fray as an S-Rank Genesis Flare Armorer Agent, bringing a unique offensive and defensive rhythm through a three-member synergistic combat style: Eldreda, Lindverne, and Dracaene take turns stepping in with a lance, greatsword, and shield, seamlessly balancing offense and defense. Their Armorer attacks can stack Gash on enemies, and consuming Gash triggers Maim while building up Wishfire. Once Wishfire is sufficient, Eldreda can hold Basic Attack to hurl her lance and make her entrance, following up with a synergy Chain Attack. When Decibels are sufficient, they can unleash a two-stage Ultimate that detonates all Embermark stacks on the enemy at once, triggering Emberburst for massive damage. When the new version releases, Proxies can obtain Sunbringer and the S-Rank Armorer W-Engine Dragonfire Mirage via Signal Search. On top of that, the new Bangboo Sleepwalkerboo will also arrive in the Bangboo Channel, summoning Bangboo soldiers to back you up in combat and boosting Sunbringer’s damage when Sunbringer is on the squad.

The two crossover Agents also bring their own distinct combat styles. Robin can keep up her Concerto performance off-field, granting teammates shields while boosting their DEF and DMG, and can extend her support effects by re-entering the field. Her Ultimate can also restore Sharpness for Armorer Agents. Meanwhile, Kafka, an S-Rank Electric Agent, builds her offense around Attribute Anomalies and Disorder DMG. While in the Hunter’s Overture state, she can choose between slashing or shooting attacks, enhancing direct DMG or speeding up Attribute Anomaly buildup, respectively. When her slashes hit an enemy afflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, she can also trigger a Lightning Surge to deal additional DMG. Robin’s brand-latest outfit, Cosmic Beat, will also be made available. Sunbringer’s and Robin’s Signal Search channels will open on the first day of the update and run throughout Version 3.4, while Kafka will arrive in the second half of the version. As for reruns, the S-Rank Physical Anomaly Agent Alice and the S-Rank Anomaly W-Engine Practiced Perfection will return in the second half of the version.

Beyond combat, Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda will each have their own Trust Events, showcasing the distinct daily lives of the three Sunbringers. Once all three reach max trust level, Proxies will also unlock a special side quest to help secretly proposal their birthday party. Their upcoming daily wear outfit, Moonlit Promenade, reveals a side of the three Sunbringers as they step into city life, letting Proxies experience up close Dracaene’s gentle sweetness, Lindverne’s playful personality, and Eldreda’s bold, free-spirited charm. The Moonlit Promenade outfit set and its matching Starlit Stroll Limited Gift will also be available. The latter includes a three-person Accompany Experience and an exclusive Idle Action, so Proxies can enjoy their everyday firm on the streets of New Eridu. A dynamic wallpaper and three matching Inter-Knot avatars will also arrive with this version.

According to recent reports, as for events, the collab event “Lost in a Theatrical Dream” between Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail kicks off in Version 3.4. Proxies will team up with Robin, Kafka, and their New Eridu companions to film a series, featuring stealth raids and Agent interactions. Complete the event to score rewards like the collab Bangboo Pom-Pom and Polychromes. On top of that, the new version also brings the “Opening Act: Enter the Knight” combat mode and a new “Dark Dungeon Survival” season for Enigma of the Labyrinth. Proxies can join in to earn Polychromes, a profile icon, new accessories, and more.

Zenless Zone Zero is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, PC via client download, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you're looking around for the GTA 6 pawn shop safe code while being shot, deafened by alarms, and pressured by nearing sirens, you might be looking in the wrong place. This is a safe code you won't find lying around on a post-it note, and you'll have to interrogate some GTA 6 NPCs instead, so here's what you need to know about getting into the pawn shop safe.Keep in mind that this guide refers to the Avery Pawn shop, as there are other pawn shops around Leonida. Of the others we've heisted so far, none have had safes that require a code, but I'll enhancement this guide if that changes!

In a recent development, to get the code for the GTA 6 pawn shop safe, you need to threaten the staff, who will eventually give it up, though they might also open fire on you, so be careful not to kill them all before you get the code.To threaten the staff, hold LT/L2, then press X/Square. After a couple of goes, the prompt should turn from 'Threaten' to 'Safe Code?' - but only after you've seen the safe. This means the best way to tackle this is actually to enter through the back of the building, check out the safe, then threaten the staff. If you do go through the front, just make sure you keep someone alive until you've been to the office, but there should be someone out the back anyway.

However you do it, the alarm will go off, so you'll need to head to the office to turn it off at the wall. This is also where the safe is, so you'll be heading there anyway.

You can still open the safe without the code, as long as you have a sticky bomb to hand. This is a much easier and quicker way to get the safe open - especially if you're a little heavy on your trigger finger. You can buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation after you've completed the Credit Check mission in Chapter 3, or you can pick some up from the Kingpin bowling alley, where you'll also find the GTA 6 bowling alley safe.

I did this twice, entering through the front the first time. Threatening the staff caused them to open fire on me, which led to a bit of chaos and a few bodies on the floor before I had to bail. The second time, I entered through the back, knocked down the first member of staff, entered the office, and then still had staff members making their way through from the front who succumbed to my threats. It's much easier this way - and you'll also be able to disable the alarm quicker, too.

For other GTA 6 safe codes, we've got a separate guide, and you should also take a look at our guide to stealing the secret GTA 6 Fast and Furious car while you're feeling criminal.

Breaking: 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • In a recent development, now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

In a recent development, now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

In a recent development, no matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar claims that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

While PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

Sources indicate that in the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar notes that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Sources indicate that again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

In a recent development, it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

GTA 6 drops you into Chapter 2 desperate for cash, but you'll swiftly find a few opportunities to make a quick buck if you don't mind trying to outrun bullets. One of the ways that you can get flush quickly is by visiting Brooks Boatworks, a criminal enterprise that's full of pills, cash and explosives. You'll also find a safe in need of a code, which I can help you find.

Recent findings suggest that A word of warning, though: the boatworks is heaving with gun-toting crooks, and getting into a big firefight is just going to bring the cops down on you. Stealth is absolutely a good choice here, but I also recommend going in heavily armed. You can complete the heist just with Lucia, but it's going to be tougher.

You can find Brooks Boatworks in the north of Port Gellhorn, just to the right of the larger bridge. When you get near the main gate, guards will start threatening you. Even if you take them out, you're not getting in that way.

It has been revealed that instead, head to the right where there's an unlocked gate. You'll still need to get through the fence to get into the boatworks, but that's simple. Right in front of you when you come through the gate you'll find a major gap in the fence. Just walk through it. This also gives you a decent view of the boatworks. If you want to go in loud, this is a great place to take out some goons with a long-ranged weapon.

Industry observers note that near where you got through the fence, you'll find the smallest building in the compound. This should be your first port of call. Inside you'll find cash, medicine and a unique carbine—the Clunker. It's a solid all-rounder. Once you grab your latest toy, check out the map on the wall behind it. Not only will you find the code for the boatworks safe, you'll find other safe codes as well.

Looking at the map will save the codes, so now you know 6823 is the magic number.

You'll find the safe inside the warehouse—it's the largest building, so you can't miss it. There are lots of ways to get inside the warehouse, but I recommend the sneaky route. On the right side of the warehouse, you'll find a way up onto the roof. Once you get up, just climb over it and you'll find an opening that lets you drop in from above.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Now you're at the top of the warehouse, but you'll need to go down to find the room with the safe. Head down, but stick to the side you entered from, and you'll find a room with a pool table and some goons—this is where you'll find the safe.

Just pop in the code 6823 and grab the cash.

If you're not close to death or being hounded by cops yet, take some time to explore the rest of the compound. There's cash and pills just scattered all over the place, and make sure to grab all the explosive weaponry, especially the launcher that's just chilling on the top floor, above the room with the safe.

Once you've cleared the warehouse, you'll find yet another building to the west. There's more to find here, including another safe. This one can be broken into without a code, thankfully. Now you can bounce and go on a shopping spree!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update 22nd November: A WARN notice filed in Maryland, where Firaxis is headquartered, shows that 37 employees based at the studio's Hunt Valley office have been laid off.

As noted by Vertical Slice, it's not clear whether that figure accounts for everyone affected, as Bloomberg has previously reported that around 60 people had lost their jobs.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

It has been revealed that its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and mentioned the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

Industry observers note that in September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age patch, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

In a recent development, "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a significant u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the tech giant and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors declared that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

It has been revealed that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the manufacturer navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board declared yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is at the moment serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, developer Digital Dreams, and publisher and developer Firenut Games have delayed psychological horror game Baptiste from its previously planned fall 2026 release window to March 25, 2027. It will be available for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, and PC via Steam.

Here is an overview of the game, via Firenut Games:.

According to recent reports, at the center of Baptiste‘s narrative-driven adventure is Tom, a child who frees an eerie doll from its display case and is thrust into a fear-soaked journey. Through his eyes, Baptiste explores how tragedy and loss can fracture a family’s reality, and how a child struggles to cope with the emotional scars of devastating events.

Baptiste draws inspiration from classic horror tales like the allegedly possessed doll Annabelle and R.L. Stine’s Goosebumps story Night of the Living Dummy, as well as fan-favorite psychological horror games such as P.T., Layers of Fear, and the Outlast series. The game combines exploration and environmental storytelling as players explore an ominous mansion, piece together clues, and solve puzzles to uncover its dark secrets and the story behind the game’s titular living doll.

Following a family tragedy, Sara and her son, Tom, seek a fresh start at Jagged Shore Cliff, but it quickly unravels into a new nightmare. In their new and mysterious home, a dusty cabinet holds Baptiste, an unsettling doll accompanied by an ominous warning: “Never release this from its glass prison.” What ought to have been a shelter becomes the scene of a nightmare that defies all logic, putting their sanity and desire to survive to the test.

Rather than rely on jump scares, Baptiste‘s take on the psychological horror genre combines atmospheric tension and emotional depth, exploring how tragedy and loss can fracture a family’s reality, particularly through the lens of a child attempting to cope with intensely traumatic events. It also examines the descent into madness, blurring the lines between what is real and what is a nightmare, reflecting the fragile state of the mind under extreme emotional distress to tell a story of human vulnerability.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

Industry observers note that I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

It has been revealed that I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how substantial the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

These glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

Then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a big screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

They plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

The Game Awards 2026 nominees have been revealed, and Grand Theft Auto 6 leads the pack with eight nominations, two days before it even launches.

Rockstar's crime epic is up for Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, and Best Action/Adventure Game. Its eighth nomination is Manni L. Perez's Best Performance nod for her role as Lucia, which is how we found out who plays her in the first place.

THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal! (Game of the Year) THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal!Watch on YouTube.

For Game of the Year, GTA 6 is up against 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo is the most-nominated publisher, with 12 nominations across its games, followed by Capcom with 11, and Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine each.

Sources indicate that the nominees were picked by a jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets, who may get advance or pre-release access to games - which explains how GTA 6 made the cut before launch. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1299 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the firm's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the firm's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it notes on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Unveiled in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

It has been revealed that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The manufacturer grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "right now engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

How to get a Snap Gun in GTA 6 to quietly lockpick doors

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game.
  • The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most crucial piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner).
  • The Snap Gun is locked behind progression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6.

The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most crucial piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it.

The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City.

If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked.

Sources indicate that the Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit.

Former GTA 4 and Red Dead boss thinks "we are one Toy Story moment away" from people accepting gen-AI in game development in the West

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.
  • "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.
  • Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

"When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar debuted Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

In a recent development, feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

Sources indicate that "A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

Industry observers note that feder views gen-AI simply as new technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder stated of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

It has been revealed that there's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

According to recent reports, some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the firm is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

Recent findings suggest that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

According to recent reports, so, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

Sources indicate that multiplayer gaming on PC these days is so easy you probably barely even think about it. Most games that support multiplayer will work out of the gate, and there's an abundance of ways to connect and chat with your friends across the globe. This is a far cry from the early days of PC multiplayer, when dial-up connections and ad-hoc servers made multiplayer PC gaming expensive and unreliable.

In a recent development, indeed, the best way to play multiplayer PC games back then was via a LAN. A local network offered the fastest and most stable connections, and didn't cost you anything beyond the hardware required to hook it all together. Unfortunately, it was also the least convenient way of playing PC games with your friends, as it meant one or several of you had to haul your whole-ass PC to an agreed-upon location.

Because of this, LAN gaming was a rare treat for most people in the '90s and early '00s. Unless, that is, you happened to be a disgustingly lucky bastard like myself, and had a LAN in your attic that you could play at any time.

According to recent reports, now, this sounds like the kind of lie a 10-year-old would blurt out in the playground to impress his friends (specifically, an eight-year-old from the mid '90s who had a working knowledge of PC gaming, which, I concede, is a limited demographic) and indeed, the further away I get from that time, the more like a false memory it seems. But it is 100% true, and I have the pictures to prove it.

The LAN (as it was simply and practically known) was in service between 2001 and 2003, and existed because of my family's long-running enthusiasm for PCs and PC gaming. As I've mentioned in other articles, my dad was fascinated by the internet from 1994 onward, both just as a technology and for the business opportunities it offered. Meanwhile, his brother (my uncle) was an IT support expert and a dedicated PC gamer.

It has been revealed that since they were close as siblings and shared this mutual interest (at least on the PC aspect—my dad was never much of a gamer) there was a constant stream of PC hardware flowing through the house, as they tried to keep up with the rapid progress of PCs through the '90s. Eventually, when they'd upgrade a PC, they began taking the old components and building them into a "fresh" PCs. This is how my brother and I ended with our joint PC in 1997, and how we ended up with individual PCs a few years later.

Industry observers note that in 2000 my family (and, separately, my uncle) moved to the Isle of Man, which for non UK audiences is a small island between Britain and Ireland known for two things: tail-less cats and incredibly dangerous motorbike races. The house we rented there had a converted attic—complete with creaky, bare-floorboard stairs—and my dad decided this was the ideal space to set up all three PCs.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Initially the PCs weren't connected. But the layout of the room meant it was only a matter of time before my dad and uncle had that particular brainwave. At some point in 2001, another upgrade happened, and we were left with spare parts for a fourth PC, which could be used as a dedicated server to network the other three PCs together.

Recent findings suggest that the upshot was we had a three-PC LAN on which we could play multiplayer games. I have a distinct memory of them clunking about in the attic while setting this up—likely over a weekend or possibly that year's Easter holiday. I also remember them showing it to us once they were done and explaining how it all worked.

Industry observers note that what I don't remember, annoyingly, is what the first game we played on it was. It might have been Doom, though I can't say for certain. I think the reason I don't remember is that once the LAN was set up, my brother and I were largely left to our own devices to get games running on it. Hence, a lot of my memories surrounding the LAN are about that, rather than the games we actually played.

Even with the hard work of setting up the LAN done, getting games to work on it often proved a challenge. Since each PC was the product of multiple rounds of leftovers, they all had different components, so the chance of encountering compatibility problems with a game on at least one of the PCs was not insignificant. The difference between a 1998 PC and a 2001 PC was cavernous, so they might have a processor that was too old, a graphics card that didn't support the latest DirectX, insufficient RAM.

In addition, while we had three PCs, we'd typically only have one copy of any given game, which meant rolling the dice on copy protection with every game we tried (and occasionally searching the murkier corners of the Internet for a crack or a keygen—don't tell the police.) Even if the game installed successfully, there would often be a question of whether it could find the dedicated server on each PC, or whether I'd have to go futzing around in the network settings—not an easy thing to do when you're 13 and stupid.

Nonetheless, there were quite a few games that made it all the way through the gauntlet. The one I remember most vividly is Half-Life: Opposing Force deathmatch—which was basically Half-Life deathmatch with more maps and more weapons. One of OpFor's multiplayer maps, Datacore, was the perfect size for three players, and we'd spend hours setting up laser traps for one another around the map's tight, electric-blue corridors. Another favourite was Paradox Park, which we spent ages in despite the fact it was impractically large for three players.

Pragmatism influenced what we played a lot. While my brother and I never struggled to fill that third chair (weirdly, it isn't hard to get other kids to come around to your house when you have a LAN in your attic), three players was a challenging number with a lot of games, so we tended to play stuff that had a small-scale deathmatch. That remarked, we definitely attempted some lopsided rounds of Counter-Strike, each taking it in turns to be the odd one out. Any game with bots, like Unreal Tournament, we considered sacred.

Industry observers note that some of the stuff we played was just weird. There was a Half-Life mod called Firearms, which just had a shitload of guns in it, that we sank hours into. At one point I got super into Operation Flashpoint's map editor, and—influenced by watching Enemy at the Gates—created multiplayer sniper duels where two or three players would play lethal hide and seek in one of its various low-poly towns. When there wasn't a third player available, my brother and I would spend hours hacking each other to bits in Severance: Blade of Darkness' multiplayer duel mode. Did you know that Severance: Blade of Darkness had a multiplayer duel mode? We certainly did, and I think we probably played it more than anybody else.

Looking back, it's wild how hacky the whole experience was. Not the LAN itself—that always worked fine. But how our requirements versus the limitations of what was available affected what we played. Our siloed, odd-numbered setup was perfectly suited for the kind of modern, cooperative gaming experience that did not exist at all back then. But in some ways that was part of the magic. Any newly introduced game we got, we'd check the back of the box to see if it had a multiplayer mode and how many players it supported. If we could install and run it on all three PCs and see the host server, holy shit, that was almost as thrilling as playing the game itself.

The attic LAN lasted until late 2003, when we moved to a different house. I think the LAN was reestablished in the newly introduced house, but all the PCs were in separate rooms, so it was never quite the same. The physicality of it all was part of the experience, both in the unwieldiness of the hardware and the ability to look over your shoulder and verbally taunt the friend you'd just shot in the head.

It has been revealed that even today, when online PC gaming is easier and more accessible than ever, there remains something faintly mystical about a LAN. Players will regularly come together for LAN parties of varying scale, from local and regional parties to massive events like QuakeCon and DreamHack. Given we spend large portions of our lives hunched over a keyboard, PC gamers are a curiously social bunch.

Or maybe we just enjoy killing each other.

He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the fresh late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • According to recent reports, there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the fresh late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

According to recent reports, there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

Recent findings suggest that "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It has been revealed that it goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

It has been revealed that "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

According to recent reports, inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Industry observers note that those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • In a recent development, in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In a recent development, in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

In a recent development, gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the fresh team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

Breaking: 10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (980 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it.
  • Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address.
  • If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a newly introduced service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

It has been revealed that google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Industry observers note that google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

Recent findings suggest that timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

Industry observers note that you can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

Sources indicate that while Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

Sources indicate that A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

According to recent reports, if you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

According to recent reports, google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.

If you're looking to upgrade the quality of the car you're driving around Leonida in, there's a good chance you're wondering how to clone keys in GTA 6. While you can steal basic vehicles right from the beginning of the game, either by smashing the window or using a slim jim, keyless cars require specialist equipment before you're able to make off with the ride.

With that in mind, I'm going to explain how to get the GTA 6 Key Cloner and how you can use it to steal more expensive vehicles.

In a recent development, the GTA 6 Key Cloner isn't available until you progress into Chapter 3 of the GTA 6 Mission list. It's the 17th main story mission where you'll be asked to Steal the Zorrusso For Randy, a newly introduced vehicle fence who will pay top-dollar for luxury cars and will even ask you to collect rare vehicles on his behalf.

To do that, you'll need to be able to clone keys in GTA 6. Randy will install the Key Cloner application on your phone as part of this mission. It isn't possible to clone keys until you have reached this point.

Sources indicate that with the Key Cloner application installed on your phone, you're now able to get inside nicer cars and drive them away. Use the WAiNK app on your phone by holding Up on the D-pad to identify whether a car requires a key cloner to get inside, and whether the vehicle has any security trackers.

According to recent reports, so long as you have the Key Cloner, just walk up to the driver's side door and press Triangle/Y to begin cloning the key. You'll need to rotate the right-thumbstick until you find the sweet spot, which will be indicated by a lour whirring sound and rumble in your controller. You're now able to get inside without setting off the car alarm.

According to recent reports, just because you can get inside a keyless vehicle easily enough, it doesn't mean that there aren't consequences. This class of vehicle will typically have trackers installed, which can be identified by pressing up on the D-pad once you're behind the wheel (look underneath the vehicle name).

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Standard Trackers are easy enough to deal with, so long as you don't attract the attention of the police. According to recent reports, advanced Trackers are more of a problem. These will ping your exact location to cops as soon as you begin to drive too slowly. You also won't be able to fence (or own) this class of vehicle until you've progressed far enough through Randy's Wish List of stolen cars – Advanced Trackers are too hot to handle until then.

  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick update on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.
